lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The résumé includes personal details that are conventionally omitted.
items.because: Date of birth and nationality do not support the technical qualifications and can distract the reader.

items.says: The résumé leaves a 10-month period unaccounted for between the bachelor's degree and the Junior Software Engineer role.
items.because: No study or work is listed between Jun 2022 and May 2023, interrupting the chronology.

items.says: Experience should appear above education.
items.because: The engineering roles carry the résumé's strongest career story.

items.says: The 35% accuracy improvement does not state its baseline, comparison, or whether it is relative or in percentage points.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the size or credibility of the improvement.

items.says: The evaluation-harness bullet does not show what changed because the regressions were caught before release.
items.because: It implies release value without making the consequence legible.

items.says: The phrase "the team used to compare" delays the stronger facts.
Assistant-only loss masking cannot make the model reproduce tool outputs more faithfully as claimed.
items.because: Tool-result tokens are excluded from the loss and receive no direct training signal.

items.says: The assistant-only loss-masking detail repeats the adapter fine-tuning accomplishment on line 9.
items.because: Repeating the method uses space without adding a second achievement.

items.says: The backlog result should say "by 68%" rather than "68%."
items.because: The missing preposition makes the reduction read less cleanly.

items.says: Switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision alone cannot account for a 4x cut in fine-tuning GPU memory.
items.because: BF16 roughly halves direct tensor storage, while fine-tuning commonly retains FP32 states, gradients, or weights.

items.says: "By 4x" lacks a baseline and does not clearly state how memory changed.
items.because: The magnitude is difficult to verify without starting and ending values.

items.says: The bullet mixes past and present tense and leads with routine maintenance instead of the improvement.
items.because: The ended role calls for consistent past tense, and the stronger contribution is easy to miss.

items.says: The three-day release-cycle result omits the prior duration.
items.because: The endpoint alone does not establish the size of the improvement.

items.says: "Automated regression checks" does not identify what the checks evaluated.
items.because: The model-release risks addressed remain unclear.

items.says: The nightly-backlog result does not quantify dispatch delays or backlog incidents.
items.because: The operational effect remains unanchored.

items.says: The 30-service event-queue migration should open the entry.
items.because: It carries the clearest operational result.

items.says: The line does not identify which AI-first practices were introduced.
items.because: The ownership claim remains abstract without the technical or organizational work performed.

items.says: "Accelerating delivery" and "improving outcomes" are unmeasured benefits.
items.because: Without a checkable result, a reader cannot assess the platform impact.

items.says: The context constraint has no stated capability, reliability, cost, or user benefit.
items.because: The bullet reads as a successful test condition rather than an outcome.

items.says: "Working context" is jargon and does not say what stayed below 10K tokens.
"Grew 100x" lacks a starting point.
items.because: The raw conversation's scale is difficult to interpret.

items.says: The method phrase does not explain which change produced the context constraint.
The claim that the changes removed nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results is too broad.
items.because: The fixes address specific failure modes but cannot guarantee that all such failures disappear.

items.says: The 50-way fan-out figure does not measure how much failures fell.
items.because: It gives test scale but no before-and-after failure count or rate.

items.says: "Under 50-way fan-out" does not clearly explain the concurrency condition.
The concurrency and cache-write bullet should open the entry.
items.because: It presents the clearest concrete reliability problem and fix.

items.says: The metric-integration bullet does not say what changed because the eight metrics were added.
items.because: The work reads as implementation without a visible result.

items.says: The line does not say what the Kendall correlation was calculated between.
items.because: The statistic is difficult to interpret without its two variables.

items.says: The trial description does not explain how the evaluator detected or scored degradation.
"Showed the evaluator tracks" is awkward.
items.because: It makes the relationship between the action and the evaluator unclear.

items.says: The evaluator bullet should open the project.
items.because: It provides the strongest measured evidence of evaluation quality.

items.says: The sensor-signal triage achievement is duplicated across entries and conflicts in ownership and reduction figure.
items.because: The same 800+ signal method appears with both a 68% and a two-thirds backlog reduction.

items.says: The two-thirds backlog reduction lacks a comparison period or baseline.
items.because: The reader cannot see how the result was calculated.

items.says: "Triage branch" may not tell a general reader what work was performed.
items.because: The implementation term hides the practical function of screening and routing cases.

items.says: "Pending-case backlog" is redundant.
items.because: Cases in a backlog are already pending.
